scope: Function contracts and named generated properties. A source-file association is not whole-file verification; direct test imports are not execution coverage.

propertyGroups.formalBoundary: Native IEEE-754 arithmetic, data views, UTF-16 operations and frozen exports remain trusted runtime boundaries.

All supported tree indices, parent/child identities and bounded ragged-tree paths are proved. Native integer guards, exact power lookup and JavaScript execution are calibrated with independent BigInt/binary oracles.
JSON, regex, object descriptors, typed arrays, aliases and chunked async input require native boundary checks.
Mutable maps, WeakRef ownership, deferred finalizers and native byte storage are not established by the pure admission proofs.

Checked production budget, pressure, projection and insertion helpers compose into bounded finite histories. Unverified admission preserves authenticated metadata and value bindings, exact byte accounting and immutable rejected states. Header admission is monotone in body size. The model assumes correct authentication flags, bounded detached metadata and owned input maps; native strict flags/keys, byte lengths and buffer ownership, serializer reentrancy, injected preparation failures, BigInt arithmetic and native Map/array identity require properties. This is a per-buffer resource and retention proof, not a signature, durable-delivery or UI-latency guarantee.

Checked expiry membership, exact retained bytes and a nondecreasing sampled clock compose with admission, removal and opaque value projection into finite histories. Failed preparations and rejected stores preserve the clock; retained receipt times are bounded by it, and successful pruning removes exactly entries whose observed age exceeds the TTL. Native safe-integer arithmetic, array/Map ownership, injected preparation failures, malformed clocks and the actual replay drain require properties. Authentication and scheduling remain assumptions; this does not prove a wall-clock deadline, periodic pruning, arbitrary-schedule replay safety or UI latency.

Sequential partition, revision, epoch, byte-budget and claim laws are proved. Promise scheduling, failures, callback side effects, rollback and native encrypted-envelope ownership require generated execution histories.
Native signing/encryption and asynchronous delegation verification are outside the proof; integrity checks do not prove cryptographic secrecy or unforgeability.
Third-party CRDT engines, native serialization and out-of-order delivery are outside the proof model.

Scalar order, lexicographic order composition and prefix-page reconstruction are proved within the model. Native IEEE-754/UTF-16 correspondence, field extraction, JSON cursors, index planning and IndexedDB still require independent full-scan and bitwise ordering oracles.
IEEE-754/int32 hashing and bitwise operations are outside the pinned model; generated merge laws and no-false-negative checks do not prove a false-positive probability.
JavaScript object identity, WeakMap ownership, prototype semantics and immutable Redux updates require runtime state histories.
Counter mutation and finite floating-point byte inputs are outside the integer-only functional proof.

The bounded retry admission decision is proved. Native transport error classification, asynchronous failure schedules, AbortSignal cancellation and diagnostic observer isolation remain runtime boundaries.

Least graph reachability, edge-linear queue bounds and ACL pruning admission are proved for detached nodes and edges. Heap traversal, CID aliases, object snapshots and descendant ACL preservation remain runtime boundaries.

Atomic reservation, exact membership append admission and uint64 epoch sequence laws are proved. Native signature verification, authority lookup, shared mutable budgets, asynchronous queues, callback failures, cancellation, fork latching and byte ownership still require generated execution histories.

Field range/trailer separation and bounded chunk-copy progress are proved. DataView endianness, native safe-integer arithmetic, typed-array offsets, Uint8ArrayList chunks, stream cleanup, canonical decoding and ownership require native malformed-input and model-calibration properties.

Exact first-eligible identity selection, digest multiplicities, strict-majority uniqueness, stable cohort projection and failure precedence are proved. Native bytes and map iteration, authority attribution, reflected probe results, Promise completion order, caller mutation and private error handling require runtime properties. Probe signatures and authorizer correctness remain caller responsibilities.

Production reservation and phase transitions have checked contracts and unbounded finite-history accounting/commit laws requiring both matching context and authorization. Promise cancellation, byte ownership, exact native closure accounting, protected anchor freshness, current-authorization guards, preparation/finalizer contracts and queue isolation remain runtime boundaries. Authentication and causal role authorization are trusted preparation obligations; this is not a whole-document or cryptographic secrecy proof.

The common stage lifecycle proves successful completion only after application succeeds and failed applications cannot be retried. Runtime callbacks and exact cleanup invocation still require calibration. Automerge immutable cloning, native missing-dependency detection, recursive callbacks, Yjs scalar/shared-type payload restrictions, escaped references, checkpoint merge/discard and constant-actor reuse require native generated execution histories.

Sequence, role, epoch advancement, journal recovery, publication-ledger insertion/projection, durable selection and finite-history provenance are proved. The Map model uses immutable values, so native Map aliasing, detached candidates, encrypted receipts, provider signatures/exporters, CRDT parsing, signed roster ownership, IndexedDB transactions, mixed crash histories and rollback-anchor conformance require native properties. These checks do not prove cryptographic primitives, network liveness or secure hardware storage.

The retained revision index accepts exactly bounded contiguous suffixes ending at the stored head with coherent minimum byte counts. Production boundedFieldEnd decisions guard native row copies; checked arbitrary finite read histories preserve exact admitted-byte sums within the declared budget, exclude zero-length copies, keep failed preparations unchanged and make failure absorbing. A batch corollary bounds accepted rows by 128. Native safe-integer guards, IndexedDB transaction/abort behavior, structured cloning, ciphertext ownership, byte-copy instrumentation and mutation during anchor awaits require properties. The proof does not bound browser structured-clone allocations, decoding buffers, total heap use or UI latency, and does not establish cryptographic authenticity or rollback-anchor honesty.

Detached roster acceptance is proved iff every entry has valid scalar fields, identities are unique and the local member exists. Successful lookup maps contain exactly the original ID/key/role bindings, retain at most 256 entries and expose no partial map on rejection. The immutable record/map model assumes owned scalar inputs. Native own-data descriptors, bounded indexed arrays, intrinsic byte copies, map independence, receiver-bound callback capture and asynchronous authorization invalidation require properties. Truthful synchronous provider guards, proxy behavior, cryptographic validity and UI latency are outside this proof; provider-boundary counterexamples are not evidence of a remote exploit.

Exact roster shape, role validity, unique identities/keys, single-controller selection and fresh bounded controller binding are proved. Checked finite histories preserve every historical controller and admit a valid signed first transition. Native Map and byte ownership, numeric calibration, canonical wire parsing, Ed25519 signatures and racing asynchronous role updates require runtime properties. A signedByCurrent proof input assumes correct authentication; cryptographic unforgeability and provider membership are not established.

Exact conflict classification, join/acceptance/index transitions, expiry projection, monotone clock and sweep frontier are proved. Checked arbitrary finite histories preserve signed join and consumed-acceptance bindings, prevent revival after expiry and bound each of four indexes by capacity. The model assumes a fixed digest-to-offer catalog, truthful validation and distinct owned maps. Native in-place Map identity, record/array ownership, canonical wire snapshots, actual SHA/signature binding, malformed clocks, immutable capacity and asynchronous digest schedules require properties. Signature verification is the caller's responsibility. This is per-instance replay memory, not a cryptographic secrecy, durable-replay or UI-latency proof; expiry sweeps remain linear in capacity.

Timestamp-window classification, monotone clock observation, exact replay retirement, immutable bounded replay admission and response eligibility are proved. A finite-history model preserves live nonces and establishes 46 retained response attempts from empty state under the 60-second lifetime, 30-second future skew and 2-second spacing. Native Map identity, signed JSON/CID framing, crypto callbacks, clock validity, post-authentication and dispatch freshness, publication failures, callback authorization and registered GossipSub verdicts independent of local response history require runtime properties. This does not prove provider correctness, UI latency, arbitrary callback liveness or durable replay protection across process restarts.

integrationBoundaries.boundary: WebRTC/libp2p, NAT/relay behavior, transport loss and browser limits
Real browser storage, restart, eviction and UI scheduling
Packed module loading, API declarations and reference applications
Malformed-input attacks, proxy/getter behavior, cancellation and cryptographic protocol assumptions not covered by a named contract/property

remainingLimits: No whole-product proof or semantic coverage percentage is claimed.
Native cryptographic entropy remains native; generated data and operation schedules have fixed seeds.
The proofs do not establish caller authentication, cryptographic secrecy, durable storage, arbitrary scheduler liveness or browser resource budgets.
Known capability gaps reported by diagnostic scenarios remain gaps.
